notes:
— Account: Sparkbridge Copilots (backend of a popular cloud IDE for mid-market teams).
— Primary ask: repository-aware copilots with sub-100ms completion streaming, ability to pin model versions per org, and strict residency for embeddings.
— Use-case detail: developer-facing IDE plugin + CI-driven code review assistant. Need repo context retrieval: embeddings + vector DB, chunking heuristics (file-level + function-level), and cold-start performance for new repos.
— POC objectives (4 weeks): 1) ingest 6 repos (300k LOC) into vector index hosted in their VPC; 2) achieve median decode latency < 120ms for single-token streaming; 3) match or exceed their current relevance baseline (MRR target in doc-search).
— Notes from discovery (2026-02-18 ff-2026-02-18-8292): "We want precise, repository-scoped results — not noisy global rank." Mentioned fallback policy: prefer recent commit context, then file-level embeddings, then global model-only fallback.
— Security & residency: security team requires SSO + SAML, SOC2 audit evidence, per-token audit logging, KMS integration for key management, and explicit geographic residency for vector storage (EU customers).
— Architecture constraints: internal CI clones repos in their VPC; prefer connector that runs in customer VPC (no code exfil). Interested in Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC peering.
— Chunking approach discussed: hybrid chunker — semantic chunk (docstring/function) up to 512 tokens + sliding window overlap for long files. Want ability to tune chunk size per repo type.
— Vector DB preferences: currently evaluating Milvus vs. Pinecone vs. self-hosted Faiss; strong preference for a vector DB that can be deployed inside their VPC. Residency requirement is the blocker for Pinecone SaaS.
— Model/version pinning: product wants predictability — must pin model family for production copilots (ability to pin v1.2.3); also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants under load.
— Streaming: literal low-latency streaming from Redwood runtime required for smooth typing experience. They emphasized signal: incremental token latency and jitter are more important than absolute throughput.
— Cost sensitivity: willing to pay for dedicated capacity for latency guarantees but want Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching + quantization to control token unit cost.

   • 2026-03-09 sample ingestion test (internal): validated chunker on two large repos; average chunk size 420 tokens; preliminary recall within expectations.
— POC success signals: MRR >= baseline + 5%, median token latency < 120ms, vector DB residency validated, SSO + audit log demo.
